ca191dd|2026-09-08|Delete the chrome-extension release plumbing from the core .github/ (#1889)
---BODY---
* Make reference-integrity's migration exemption reach real records

The exemption filtered for a top-level migrations/<slug>/migration.mjs and
read only the records the change itself edits. Every record lives under the
pack or engine that owns it, and a branch deleting a vendored-out path is
exactly the branch that does not touch the record describing the vendoring,
so the exemption selected nothing on every run.

Fixes #1888

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01JDM5zctVqPMAvCYjTY14j6

* Delete the chrome-extension release plumbing from the core .github/

The pack has held these as templates since the chrome-release-vendoring
migration, and every consumer now runs its own vendored copy, so the four
reusable workflows and the two composite actions only they used have no
caller left. report-failure stays: the scheduler here and every member stub
call it @main.

A record's codemod rewrites files the member owns, and the member's own tests
assert on them in a repo this canon has never seen. Twice now that landed a
member whose declarations are current and whose tests pin the generation

of the mount as a stated design property, and no rehearsal fixture carries a
task test, so both converge green against a declaration nothing in them
asserts on.

the other's: assertApplyStageDeclaration throws on an engine record declaring
applyStage, so that finding names relocation to the owning pack instead — the
registry's own error text for the case.

that write a member's task.json and nothing else, 2 of the corpus's 27 records.
`rewrite` stays out — it is most records' workhorse, and firing on it would
make every migration a migration question.

load-bearing by weakening it and watching a test redden — dropping the path
filter reddens two, dropping the base dedupe, the comment stripping and the
applyStage discharge one each — since a case asserting a guard yields nothing
passes from birth. Replayed against both real records, it fires on each and
hands each the remedy its flow allows.

Closes #1858

load-bearing by weakening it and watching a test redden — dropping the path
filter reddens two, dropping the base dedupe, the comment stripping and the
applyStage discharge one each — since a case asserting a guard yields nothing
passes from birth. Replayed against both real records, it fires on each and
hands each the remedy its flow allows.

Closes #1858

entries.name: mcp__github__actions_get
entries.description:
Get details about specific GitHub Actions resources.
Use this tool to get details about individual workflows, workflow runs, jobs, and artifacts by their unique IDs.

resource_id.description:
The unique identifier of the resource. This will vary based on the "method" provided, so ensure you provide the correct ID:
- Provide a workflow ID or workflow file name (e.g. ci.yaml) for 'get_workflow' method.
- Provide a workflow run ID for 'get_workflow_run', 'get_workflow_run_usage', and 'get_workflow_run_logs_url' methods.
- Provide an artifact ID for 'download_workflow_run_artifact' method.
- Provide a job ID for 'get_workflow_job' method.

entries.name: mcp__github__actions_list
entries.description:
Tools for listing GitHub Actions resources.
Use this tool to list workflows in a repository, or list workflow runs, jobs, and artifacts for a specific workflow or workflow run.

perPage.description: Results per page for pagination (default: 30, max: 100)

resource_id.description:
The unique identifier of the resource. This will vary based on the "method" provided, so ensure you provide the correct ID:
- Do not provide any resource ID for 'list_workflows' method.
- Provide a workflow ID or workflow file name (e.g. ci.yaml) for 'list_workflow_runs' method, or omit to list all workflow runs in the repository.
- Provide a workflow run ID for 'list_workflow_jobs' and 'list_workflow_run_artifacts' methods.

filter.description: Filters jobs by their completed_at timestamp

workflow_jobs_filter.description: Filters for workflow jobs. **ONLY** used when method is 'list_workflow_jobs'

actor.description: Filter to a specific GitHub user's workflow runs.

branch.description: Filter workflow runs to a specific Git branch. Use the name of the branch.

event.description: Filter workflow runs to a specific event type

status.description: Filter workflow runs to only runs with a specific status

workflow_runs_filter.description: Filters for workflow runs. **ONLY** used when method is 'list_workflow_runs'

entries.name: mcp__github__actions_run_trigger
entries.description: Trigger GitHub Actions workflow operations, including running, re-running, cancelling workflow runs, and deleting workflow run logs.

inputs.description: Inputs the workflow accepts. Only used for 'run_workflow' method.

ref.description: The git reference for the workflow. The reference can be a branch or tag name. Required for 'run_workflow' method.

run_id.description: The ID of the workflow run. Required for all methods except 'run_workflow'.

workflow_id.description: The workflow ID (numeric) or workflow file name (e.g., main.yml, ci.yaml). Required for 'run_workflow' method.

entries.name: mcp__github__get_job_logs
entries.description:
Get logs for GitHub Actions workflow jobs.
Use this tool to retrieve logs for a specific job or all failed jobs in a workflow run.
For single job logs, provide job_id. For all failed jobs in a run, provide run_id with failed_only=true.

failed_only.description: When true, gets logs for all failed jobs in the workflow run specified by run_id. Requires run_id to be provided.

job_id.description: The unique identifier of the workflow job. Required when getting logs for a single job.

return_content.description: Returns actual log content instead of URLs

run_id.description: The unique identifier of the workflow run. Required when failed_only is true to get logs for all failed jobs in the run.

tail_lines.description: Number of lines to return from the end of the log

content.content:
Sweep per-pack task tests to stop re-proving the task mechanism (#1820)
Each pack's tasks.test.mjs asserted things the scheduler's own suite
already proves for every declaration — validateTaskDeclaration(decl)
empty, taskCadence/preconditionSignals equalling a literal, a built-in
term holding or declining on a plain declaration. Trim those, keeping
only what proves a pack's own code: a task-local term's decisions, a
worker's behaviour, a merge-rules verdict, a two-artifact drift claim,
or a composed `||` expression the pack designed.

packs/tidy-repo/test/pack.test.mjs is deleted whole — every assertion
in it drove only built-in terms (issues-touched, prs-touched) already
covered in claudinite-tasks/test/precondition-policy.test.mjs.

Adds one bullet to writing-tests/SKILL.md stating the rule.

Refs #1774

git log --since=2026-09-05 --format=$'\x01%H\x02%cI\x02%an\x02%s\x02%b' > /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claudinite/a5933e64-2fa8-582e-ac4e-6aa5b25996db/scratchpad/log.txt; python3 - <<'PY'
import re,subprocess
p='/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claudinite/a5933e64-2fa8-582e-ac4e-6aa5b25996db/scratchpad/log.txt'
raw=open(p).read().split('\x01')
HOUSE=re.compile(r'\[skip ci\]|(^|\n)\s*baselin(e|ing)\b|claudinite[ -](baselin|maintenance|growth|task|work)|seed default-on',re.I)
for e in raw:
    if not e.strip(): continue
    sha,cI,an,subj,body=(e.split('\x02')+['']*5)[:5]
    msg=subj+'\n\n'+body
    files=subprocess.run(['git','show','--name-only','--format=','-m','--first-parent',sha],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout.split()
    trailer=re.search(r'^Claudinite-Task:\s*(\S+)',body,re.M)
    bot=an.endswith('[bot]')
    corpus=len(files)>0 and all(f.startswith('.claudinite/') for f in files)
    house=bool(HOUSE.search(msg))
    subst=not(bot or trailer or corpus or house)
    why=[k for k,v in (('bot',bot),('trailer',bool(trailer)),('corpus',corpus),('house',house)) if v]
    print(f"{sha[:7]} {cI} subst={str(subst):5} why={','.join(why) or '-':28} {subj[:60]}")
PY

A record's codemod rewrites files the member owns, and the member's own tests
assert on them in a repo this canon has never seen. Twice now that landed a
member whose declarations are current and whose tests pin the generation
before: #768 Phase 1's normalizeLocalDeclarations against Shepherd's worker and
task test, and #1725's updateTaskSchedulingFields against five gcec tests.

The second record said so outright — "No apply stage: the rewrite is text, and
a session has nothing to add." The text was the easy half; the half no codemod
reaches is running the member's suite and repairing what pinned the old shape.

Neither consumer gate can see it. The canary's local pack imports nothing out
of the mount as a stated design property, and no rehearsal fixture carries a
task test, so both converge green against a declaration nothing in them
asserts on.

The remedy splits by flow, because one of the two records could not have taken
the other's: assertApplyStageDeclaration throws on an engine record declaring
applyStage, so that finding names relocation to the owning pack instead — the
registry's own error text for the case.

Narrow on purpose, the bargain consumer-safe-change strikes: the two codemods
that write a member's task.json and nothing else, 2 of the corpus's 27 records.
`rewrite` stays out — it is most records' workhorse, and firing on it would
make every migration a migration question.

Eleven tests, red before the module existed. Each guard was then proved
load-bearing by weakening it and watching a test redden — dropping the path
filter reddens two, dropping the base dedupe, the comment stripping and the
applyStage discharge one each — since a case asserting a guard yields nothing
passes from birth. Replayed against both real records, it fires on each and
hands each the remedy its flow allows.

Closes #1858

{"number":1849,"title":"`INCLUDE_DORMANT=true` is a no-op — the scheduler's dormancy gate runs before the forced wake","body":"## What happens

`force-fleet-baseline.mjs` offers `INCLUDE_DORMANT=true` as the operator's way to reach a member that stopped its own scheduler. It is documented in the pack's `README.md`, its `RULES.md` and the task's own README, and the worker threads it through as `FLEET_BASELINE_INCLUDE_DORMANT`.

It does nothing. Passing it skips the enforcer-side filter and fires `claudinite-scheduler.yml` on the dormant member — and that run stops at its own dormancy gate in `scheduler-run.mjs` (`main()`), which returns before the forced-wake block near the end of the same function reads `CLAUDINITE_WAKE`. The wake is never planned, no item is minted or woken, and nothing converges.

The sweep reports the member under `fired`, because a dispatch that returns 204 is all it observed. So the operator's override reports success for work that never happened — a config channel that has stopped being read and defaults silently, which is the failure mode the repo's own rule about dispatch parameters exists to prevent.

## Why it matters now

#1845 makes the roster measure dormant members and report a mount that has fallen behind canon. That signal is deliberately advisory — the routine fan-out still leaves dormant members alone — and the stated ways to clear it are to wake the repo or to run an explicit include-dormant baseline. Only the first of those actually works today.

## The shape of the fix

Dormancy means **no recurring work** — that is what the predicate's own documentation says it covers. An operator's explicit `wake` naming a task is not recurring work: it is a person asking for one specific thing, once. So the gate should distinguish the two rather than treat every entry into the run identically:

- a cron tick on a dormant member does nothing, exactly as now;
- a run carrying an explicit `CLAUDINITE_WAKE` spec performs that wake and nothing else — no instantiation of other due tasks, no ready sweep, no reclaim, since those are the recurring work the declaration stopped.

That keeps the declaration's promise intact while giving the override a real channel, and it needs no change to the vendored workflow stub: `wake` is already an input and already reaches the run as an environment variable.

input.title: A forced wake ignores `taskScheduler.disabledTasks` and runs a task the repo turned off
input.body:
## What happens

`planSchedulerRun` reads `taskScheduler.disabledTasks` and skips a named task before it is ever asked (`packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/scheduler-run.mjs:95`, `:129`), and it closes a *blocked* item that names one (`:120`). The forced-wake path does neither: `planWake(spec, tasks, current)` (`:726`) is handed the discovered task list and no schedule at all, so `disabledTasks` is never consulted. A `wake` naming a disabled task resolves its owner, finds no open standing item, mints one **ready** (`:739`), and the `drain` job dispatches an executor for it. The retire-orphan branch cannot catch it either — it is scoped to `STATUS_BLOCKED`, and a minted wake item is `READY`.

So the per-task off switch holds for every cron tick and fails for exactly the lever built to reach a member from outside: the fleet enforcer dispatches `claudinite-scheduler.yml` with the task ids it wants run now, and a member that declared a task off still runs it.

Read live on this repository: `claudinite-growth/logs-prune` is in `.claudinite-settings.json`'s `disabledTasks`, and the scheduler-run logs of 2026-09-09T10:05Z and 10:16Z ask every other declared task and never name it. Nothing in `planWake` would stop a `wake: claudinite-growth/logs-prune` from minting one anyway.

## Why it is not academic here

That wake is the only route to a live evaluation of `log-past-retention`, which is why #1579's phase-3 read of a task-local term is stuck. Taking it would not have been a read-only probe: `resolveRetentionDays(undefined)` returns `DEFAULT_RETENTION_DAYS` (10), not `null` (`packs/claudinite-growth/tasks/logs-prune/prune-logs.mjs:40`), so an unset `retention_days` is the default window rather than capture-only, the term can hold, and the worker deletes capture files on a task this repo switched off. A disabled task's side effects are the reason the switch exists.

## The shape of the fix

`planWake` should take the schedule the way `planSchedulerRun` does and report a disabled id in `unmatched`, with the reason naming `taskScheduler.disabledTasks` — which also makes the run exit non-zero, so a fleet force that named a disabled task says so rather than reporting coverage it did not have.

Worth deciding beside #1849, which argues the opposite direction for the *dormancy* gate: an explicit wake should override "this repo does no recurring work", and should not override "this repo does not run this task". The two gates answer different questions and the wake path currently honours neither.

_Filed by the Claudinite task `claudinite-tasks/implement-request`, running as work item missingbulb/Claudinite#1579 — no person asked for this issue._

## Phase 3 (#1579): three more reads off real runs, one blocked

Readiness first: the canon's own scheduler runs carry the new evaluator — every tick since the merge prints the `- asked <pack>/<task>: go|no|fail-open — <reason>` lines `scheduler-run.mjs` composes from `precondition-policy.mjs`, and the two runs quoted below are on head shas `f6c260b` and `ffecb75`. The member-stamp half of "ready when" is not readable from a session scoped to this repository; nothing below depends on it.

### ✅ Read 1 — a movement-gated task declines on a quiet window, via a forced wake

`workflow_dispatch` on `claudinite-scheduler.yml` with `wake: claudinite-growth/growth-extract` — [run 34339340764](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/34339340764), 2026-09-09T10:16Z, head `ffecb75`:

```
- asked claudinite-growth/growth-extract: no — no substantive default-branch change in the window
- created #1903 claudinite-growth/growth-extract (forced: it had no open standing item)
```

The mint carries `Woken: 2026-09-09T10:16:40.782Z`, so at pick `due:daily` held on the wake and `substantive-change` was the sole decider. The executor's converge on #1903:

```
The precondition declined: no substantive default-branch change in the window

This task is asked again at the next scheduler run; a decline is recorded nowhere but here.

claudinite-task-exec v1 claudinite-growth/growth-extract [#1903] success
```

Closed `task:status:rejected` / `not_planned`, record `success`. The wake-that-finds-no-work verdict, not a failure — and the wake isolated the movement term exactly as designed.

### ✅ Read 2 — the same task runs on an active window, Context carrying the term's scope

[Run 34213408097](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/34213408097), 2026-09-08T10:04Z:

```
- asked claudinite-growth/growth-extract: go — no run since the daily anchor at 2026-09-08T05:00:00.000Z; 1 substantive default-branch commit(s) in the window
- created #1894 claudinite-growth/growth-extract [task:origin:planned task:status:waiting-for-executor]
```

#1894's body carries `substantive-change`'s own `cappedContext` line, and nothing else:

```
### Context

- Substantive commits in the window: ca191dd.
```

It ran to `task:status:done`, delivering PR #1898 (`76e0b72`). The two-part reason composes cleanly across the conjunction, and the go verdict's context reaches the item the way the design says.

### ✅ Read 5 — the machinery's own landed output leaves the repo silent

Same window, two terms, opposite verdicts — [run 34338269306](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/34338269306), 2026-09-09T10:05Z:

```
- asked claudinite-growth/growth-extract: no — no substantive default-branch change in the window
- asked claudinite-tasks/usage-fold: go — no run since the daily anchor at 2026-09-09T05:00:00.000Z; 3 default-branch commit(s) in the window
```

Both tasks last ran a second apart on 2026-09-08T10:04, so both windows hold the same three commits: `5243da3` (`Claudinite-Task: claudinite-tasks/usage-fold`), `76e0b72` (`Claudinite-Task: claudinite-growth/growth-extract`) and `f6c260b`. Three commits landed on `main`; `any-commit` counted three and `substantive-change` counted none. `76e0b72` is growth-extract's *own* delivery, and it did not re-arm growth-extract on the following window — which is the claim.

One caveat for the retrospective rather than against the read: **no live log line can ever attribute this to the trailer alone.** All three commits in that window are also corpus-only (`.claudinite/…`), and `Claudinite-Task:` itself matches the `HOUSEKEEPING` regex (`claudinite[ -]task`), which is tested against the whole message — so a stamped commit trips at least two exclusions by construction. In code the trailer branch runs first and returns before the others (`packs/claudinite-tasks/signals/index.mjs:63`); from outside, the exclusions are only ever observable together.

### ❌ Read 4 — blocked, and its stated premise is wrong

`claudinite-growth/logs-prune` is named in this repository's `taskScheduler.disabledTasks`, so `planSchedulerRun` skips it before it is ever asked — it appears in no `asked` line of any run. `log-past-retention` therefore never evaluates live here, on any tick.

The one route left is a forced wake, and it is not safe to take. #1579 scoped this read down on the premise that "the canon leaves `retention_days` unset, so the live read available here is the term's unset-retention decline". That premise does not hold: `resolveRetentionDays(undefined)` returns `DEFAULT_RETENTION_DAYS` (10), not `null` — unset is the *default window*, not capture-only. So the term can hold on a wake, and the worker would delete capture files on a task this repo switched off. I stopped rather than take that read.

That the wake would run it at all is its own defect, filed as #1904: `planWake` is handed no schedule and never consults `disabledTasks`, so the per-task off switch holds for every cron tick and fails for the fleet-facing lever. Worth reading beside #1849, which argues the opposite direction for the dormancy gate.

**A task-local term did evaluate live today**, if a substitute read is acceptable: `growth-promote`'s `fleet-local-packs-changed` failed open at the tick (no `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` in the scheduler job) and was decided by the executor at pick — #1899, closed `task:status:rejected`:

```
The precondition declined: no participating member changed its local packs in the window
```

That exercises the task-local resolution path, the fail-open→decide-at-pick handoff, and a term-composed reason. It does not exercise `log-past-retention`'s age arithmetic, which stays covered by `logs-prune`'s unit tests.

### One drift note on read 3

Read 3 is recorded as "a `['none']` task (`task-janitor`) runs unconditionally as before". `none` has since been retired — `parsePreconditions` errors on it (`precondition-policy.mjs:41`) — and `task-janitor` now declares `['due:daily']`. The behaviour still reads true today (`- asked claudinite-tasks/task-janitor: go — no run since the daily anchor at 2026-09-09T05:00:00.000Z` → #1900); only the read's description of the declaration is stale.

### Where phase 3 stands

Reads 1, 2, 3 and 5 are quoted off real runs. Read 4 needs a decision: accept the `fleet-local-packs-changed` substitute, or re-scope it once #1904 makes a wake of a disabled task refuse. #1579 stays open.
